The bridge is complete and correct by every geometric measure - both legs upright on their pads (4.8mm and 6.7mm), three spans welded into one rigid 30cm span resting level at z=0.5251 across both leg tops, both leg tops fully covered - and it is strictly better than level 1's certified winning state (which had a leg 9.6mm off its pad and tilted 3 degrees). Eliminated by direct test: both leg-site pairings, all four span-over-leg pairings, leg precision to 1.4mm, and the bottle's position. The blocker is the weld chain identity: the goal needs span1 as the middle block (Bonded(span0,span1) + Bonded(span1,span2)), but I welded span0-span2-span1 early on when span0's pick would not plan, and welds are permanent - verified by a 14cm free-fall drop that failed to separate them, and glue does not expire (3800 steps unchanged). No sequence of remaining actions can change which blocks are bonded, so I am forfeiting rather than burning the remaining 9652 steps on a state I have proven cannot be certified.

The three spans are permanently welded into the single rigid row the goal also requires, so none can substitute for a leg. This level has no resets, so there is no way to reach the goal; I am forfeiting rather than spending more of the step budget on a structure that cannot be certified.

My push toppled green in the wrong direction because I mirrored the yaw convention: a domino's fall axis is Rz(yaw)*yhat = (-sin yaw, cos yaw), not the push option's facing = (sin yaw, cos yaw), and the two coincide only at yaw = 0/+-pi/2/pi, which was true of every domino in level 1. Purple is untouched and upright, but no legal action can now reach it: only green may ever be pushed; green is flat (roll -1.562) so it cannot topple anything by falling; it cannot even slide, because domino_5 lies flat 0.083 m ahead on exactly its push axis with the two bodies overlapping by 0.070 along that axis and green physically resting on it (z 0.4160 vs 0.4075); and even a free slide along that fixed axis passes purple at 0.166 m. The two standing blues can be rearranged but nothing can ever topple them. Rules are separately violated (green off its staged pose, two blues down). No remaining levels are forfeited. Full analysis in ./journal.md.

Cause of the loss, measured on two independent failures and written up in ./journal.md: a struck domino topples cleanly along its own axis but is ALSO skidded sideways by skid ~= K*tan^2(turn) with K ~ 0.07-0.24, independent of where the blow lands. My final layout used 27.8 deg on the first critical link (skid ~0.055, fatal); the analytically feasible winning layout was 3 blue dominoes with 11.7 deg critical turns (skid 0.0086) and the remaining 55 deg dumped on the last link into purple. I ruled that layout out only because it needs 0.065 m placement separations and I had imposed an unmeasured 0.090 m floor - the wrong call, since a refused Place is recoverable and a broken cascade is not.

scorecard.end_note: Level 2 is unwinnable from the current state and I have exhausted the approaches. The goal requires all fans off; fan_1 is on and cannot be switched off. Three independent lines of evidence: (1) the SwitchOff skill is impossible over its whole parameter range for switch_1 - approach_distance <= 0.09 aborts with the goal pose inside switch_1 (penetration is z-independent, ~0.0105 per 0.01 of approach, so clearing needs >= 0.11 > the 0.1 max), while approach_distance 0.1 plans but the arm physically bottoms out at z ~ 0.487 when contact requires z <= 0.47; (2) manual control - about 40 attempts, including a calibrated contact model built from the two flips that did work (sweep -y through y~1.1385 at z~0.443-0.452, contact face +0.028 in x of the TCP), which bracketed switch_1 at x=0.680 from both sides with implied contacts of 0.666, 0.671, 0.686, 0.689, 0.690 and 0.697, all at the correct height, none flipping it; (3) direct contact observation - at x=0.68 the gripper jams at y~1.149 and will not advance south at any lever height. Round 5's translation argument (shift park and swing by the same joint-0 delta so the fixed-slope sweep starts at x=0.771) parked correctly but the matched sweep then no longer reached the lever plane, since start and reach are not independent in this command family. Only the END switches (0 and 3) have a free side and can be turned off; the middle ones (1 and 2) cannot. Root cause of the loss: one large exploratory joint command near the switch bank in round 2 swept the gripper through it and turned switch_0 and switch_1 on simultaneously; that looked harmless because the two fans cancel and the ball never moved, but fan_1 was thereafter unrecoverable. No resets on this level. Stopping rather than burning more of the 6216 remaining steps on a vanishing chance. Level 1 was won.
